name: Thunee
description: Thunee (or Thuni) is a popular trick-taking card game in South Africa, particularly among Indian South Africans in Durban. It is related to the Jass family of games (like 304). The name 'Thunee' means 'water' in Tamil (though the connection is debated) or refers to a specific call. Unusually, the Jack and Nine are the highest cards. The game involves bidding and 'ball' scoring.

history.origins: Evolved from the '304' game brought by Indian indentured labourers to South Africa.
timeline: 19th century: Brought to South Africa by Indian indentured labourers; evolved into Thunee in Durban.
history.cultural: A central part of social life in Durban's Indian community.
history.evolution: Developed its own distinctive terminology (Balls, Khanock, Thunee call).

rules.objective: Win tricks to score points (Balls). First to 12/13 Balls wins.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal 4. 2. Bidding (10, 20, etc., or Thunee). Highest bidder sets Trump. 3. Deal 2. 4. Play tricks. Must follow suit. Trumping allowed if void. 5. Scoring: Card values: J=30, 9=20, A=11, 10=10, K=3, Q=2. Total 104 points (plus bonus?).

strategy.basic: Similar to 304: Save Jacks and Nines. Secure trumps early.
strategy.intermediate: Counting points to reach 105 (winning total?). Signalling partner.
strategy.advanced: Bluffing with a Thunee call. Catching a Thunee (stopping them).

scoring.description: Teams score 'Balls' based on points taken vs bid. 'Thunee' call wins 4 balls if successful (all tricks). 'Khanock' is a double penalty.
